These are small learning experiments, each asking one question. Open a page
for its task, visible behavioral criteria, comparison, and recorded result.
Plain readouts and structured tables show the selected measurements;
provenance and runnable code are available in the details tabs.

The catalog includes the required core suite and separately provisioned research
studies. Research pages are labeled beside their result badge and list their
wheel, optional dependency, or offline model requirements in Reproduce. A newly
defined experiment stays Missing until a full recorded result is selected.

Read each page as a worked question. The model receives some information and
must infer an answer that has been hidden from it. Because the examples are
generated from a known rule, we can check both the answer and the information
needed to find it. A comparison then changes something specific—such as
removing an identity match or hiding a useful input—to test that explanation.

They test specific mechanisms in models generated from declared field types,
nested structures, and objectives: what information survives encoding, what
the model can learn, and how learned state behaves during reuse or edits.
The measurements describe those controlled setups. They do not establish
application quality, competitive benchmark rankings, or production training
and serving throughput. The [use cases](use-cases/index.qmd) show how to
design and evaluate a workload around a real decision.

Three approachable starting points:

- [Adding six numbers](evidence/structure/attention-learns-fixed-width-sum.html):
  can a model recover a total from six visible values? The page distinguishes
  learning an approximate calculation from guaranteeing exact arithmetic.
- [Matching unfamiliar IDs](evidence/identity/unseen-identity-equality.html):
  can it recognize that two new labels are the same, even when neither label
  occurred in training? Matching is different from understanding what a name means.
- [Distinguishing missing values from zero](evidence/state/null-versus-zero.html):
  a recorded zero and an absent reading carry different information. What
  happens when a preprocessing step replaces both with zero?


The catalog is ordered by group, from simple aggregation to calibration and
anomaly detection. Search or sort by question, group, result, or ID, such as
`P021`.

::: {#evidence}
:::

<details>
<summary>How to read the results</summary>

These experiments measure behavior on controlled synthetic data. Each result
applies to its recorded setup. A successful run can be provisional. Some experiments are
designed to demonstrate a limitation. Short execution checks, called smoke
runs, do not replace full learning results.

| Result | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| [Passing]{.evidence-status data-evidence-status="Passing"} | The current full run meets its stated checks. |
| [Failing]{.evidence-status data-evidence-status="Failing"} | The current full run misses at least one required check. |
| [Error]{.evidence-status data-evidence-status="Error"} | The current full run could not complete. |
| [Missing]{.evidence-status data-evidence-status="Missing"} | No full run has been recorded. |

Each page shows one selected full run, with its measurements, checks, seed,
and source provenance. Publication retains selected complete CI runs as
[run reports](https://github.com/relflow/relflow/releases) in the package
repository. Each published selection links its retained paired execution
records. A single seed provides provisional evidence about repeatability;
internal seed panels are described by each experiment.

| Term | How to read it |
| --- | --- |
| Input | A field the model may use when making a prediction. |
| Target | The answer used for training or scoring; the schema controls whether the model can see it as an input. |
| Held-out example | An observation reserved for evaluation rather than the training updates being scored. |
| Control | A comparison that changes a specific source of information or model behavior. It helps explain why an apparent success occurs. |
| Metric | A numerical measurement, such as prediction error or agreement with known groups. |
| Check | A declared condition on behavior or measurements. A threshold crossing answers one specific question. |
| Normalized RMSE | Prediction error divided by the experiment's stated reference error. Lower is better; the page identifies the reference. |
| ARI | Agreement between two ways of grouping the same items. One means the groupings match, zero is chance-level agreement, and cluster names do not matter. |

For example, if a page normalizes error against a constant guess, an error
ratio of `0.25` means one quarter of that guess's RMSE. It does not mean
25% classification accuracy. Similarly, recovering several clusters does
not establish that the clusters match the true groups; that is what ARI checks.

Learned arithmetic is approximate. Use
[preprocessing](guides/preprocessing.qmd) for business rules that require exact results.
Each page includes its reproduction command and a downloadable script.

</details>
